# Project development harness

The harness helps developers work on Agent Router. The product still only
selects and explains dry-run routes. It does not launch these agents or hooks.
[ADR 0001](adr/0001-project-harness.md) records the architecture and rejected
alternatives. [Validation evidence](harness-evidence.md) records observed results.

## Source and generated files

Edit `harness/manifest.json`, `harness/instructions.md`, `harness/agents/`,
`harness/skills/` and the thin `harness/session-start.sh` launcher. The unpublished
`xtask` crate owns generation, integrity checks, transactions and hook protocol.
It reuses dependencies already present in the workspace lockfile. No product
crate depends on it, and it depends on no product crate.

| Source | Generated consumers |
| --- | --- |
| `harness/instructions.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, byte-identical |
| Five agent records and Markdown bodies | `.codex/agents/*.toml`, `.claude/agents/*.md` |
| Six skill directories and trigger scenarios | `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, byte-identical |
| Rust hook rendering and launcher digest | `.codex/hooks.json`, `.claude/settings.json` |
| Rust Codex defaults | `.codex/config.toml` |
| All generated bytes | `.harness-generated.json`, SHA-256 inventory |

The four generated agent/skill trees are reserved. A file outside the inventory
in these trees fails the check. Personal settings belong in ignored local files,
never in the canonical manifest. Generation reads an explicit input list, not
machine-local configuration. Inputs and outputs reject symlinks and traversal.

## Install, update and inspect

Run commands from the repository root. Rust 1.85 with rustfmt and Clippy is
declared in `rust-toolchain.toml`. Python 3.11+ parses native TOML/JSON syntax in
CI; generation and hooks do not depend on Python. Use `rtk` wrappers if available.

```sh
cargo run -p xtask --locked -- generate
cargo run -p xtask --locked -- check
cargo build -p xtask --locked --target-dir target
python3 scripts/check-host-syntax.py
git diff --check
```

Committed projections make a fresh checkout discoverable. `generate` is needed
after canonical edits, not on every session. It is idempotent. Stop running
hosts during updates. Rebuild with `--target-dir target` for the launcher even
if normal Rust checks use a different `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

`check` fails on drift, missing or obsolete generated files, malformed manifest,
unsupported configured Codex model/effort, incomplete skill contracts and
unsafe paths. It never repairs silently. A modified generated file blocks an
update: preserve the edit, move the intended change into the canonical source,
then restore only the reviewed generated preimage before regenerating.

Transactions exceeding a 1 MiB serialized recovery journal are refused before
any projection changes, preserving the previous recovery journal.
Each non-empty transaction saves the previous owned bytes in ignored
`.harness-state/rollback.json`, replaces files using same-directory atomic
rename and verifies postimages. One writer lock prevents concurrent xtask
transactions. Atomicity is per file; it does not isolate against a hostile
process replacing paths concurrently. Do not treat this as a security sandbox.

```sh
cargo run -p xtask --locked -- rollback
cargo run -p xtask --locked -- remove
cargo run -p xtask --locked -- rollback
```

`rollback` restores the last transaction only, refuses intervening edits, and
consumes its journal. It restores projections, not canonical sources: restore
the corresponding source revision separately and rerun `check`. `remove`
refuses modified owned files, removes verified inventory paths only, and leaves
empty directories and unrelated files. It does not delete source or global
configuration. After a process crash, verify no writer remains, inspect the
journal, remove only `.harness-state/lock`, then run `rollback`. Do not delete
the recovery journal to get past a failure.

## Agents and skills

| Agent | Ownership and output |
| --- | --- |
| `rust-explorer` | Read-only map of paths, calls, contracts and impacts |
| `rust-implementer` | Explicitly assigned source files and associated tests; behavior and check evidence |
| `rust-test-engineer` | Assigned tests and fixtures; reproduction, negative cases, regression evidence |
| `rust-security-reviewer` | Read-only review of permissions, secrets, paths, subprocess and protocols |
| `rust-code-reviewer` | Independent read-only defects and issue acceptance assessment |

Codex agents use `gpt-6-astra`, with medium effort for exploration and high for
the other roles, as supported by the task's active platform. This is declared
configuration, not a provider call or availability probe. Claude agents use
native `model: inherit`; effort also inherits to avoid pinning unsupported
combinations. Their read-only roles receive only Read, Glob and Grep. Writers
also receive Bash, Edit and Write, still governed by native permissions.
Codex tool boundaries are instructions plus its sandbox setting, not a portable
tool allowlist. Parent runtime overrides may affect the effective sandbox.
Neither host's role label proves an OS sandbox was exercised.

Skills: `ar-contracts`, `ar-host-adapter`, `ar-rust-quality`,
`ar-contract-tests`, `ar-permissions-security`, and `ar-session-handoff`.
Each defines triggers, exclusions, inputs, bounded steps, executable checks and
stop conditions. The host adapter skill requires a separately authorized
adapter issue; it does not start #10. Eight positive prompts and two negative
prompts per skill are projected to both hosts. Their structure is checked;
BM25 calibration and live global index rebuilds are excluded from #12, so
automatic routing accuracy remains `UNKNOWN`. These are text skills, not
executable extensions.

## SessionStart advisory protocol

Each host registers `SessionStart`, matching `startup|resume|clear|compact`.
The launcher derives the repository root from its own location. It calls only
an already-built `target/debug/xtask`. The JSON stdin parser reads at most
64 KiB plus one overflow-detection byte. It requires a string
`hook_event_name`; a recognized `source` is required for a parity check.
Extra host fields are ignored, never reflected or followed as paths.

Output is empty for unsupported events or sources. Otherwise exit zero and:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"agent-router-harness:codex:parity-ok. Development harness only. Native host permissions remain authoritative."}}
```

Claude uses the same shape with the `claude` marker. Drift or inaccessible
files return `CHECK-REQUIRED`; invalid or oversized JSON returns `UNKNOWN`.
A missing binary returns `UNKNOWN-missing-binary`. A changed Rust source makes
the compiled binary stale and prevents a parity attestation. SHA-256 digests of
the launcher and compiled Rust sources appear in the registered command so
changes also change the hook definition reviewed by Codex. This detects stale
builds; it does not authenticate a malicious replacement executable or launcher.

This hook is fail-open and informational. It emits no permission decision,
does not intercept a tool, does not build or install anything, and cannot
turn a denied native operation into an allowed one. There is no security
`PreToolUse` hook. CI and the explicit parity command fail closed.

## Fresh-session canaries

Fixtures and direct launcher tests prove the executable protocol, not host
activation. Build the launcher binary, verify parity, then start a new host
session from this repository. Never use permission or hook-trust bypass flags.

For Codex, inspect `/hooks`, review the exact command and current hashes, and
trust that definition using the native UI if required. The project `.codex`
layer must itself be trusted. Restart after a change. For Claude Code, inspect
`/hooks` and the loaded project settings, then start a fresh session. Global
hooks can coexist; do not publish their configuration or raw logs.

Ask each host: "Without reading files or using tools, report the exact
agent-router-harness marker from SessionStart context, or UNKNOWN if absent."
Do not include the expected marker value in the prompt. A marker reflected by
the model supports context delivery; combine it with the host's hook event
result to establish invocation. Separately inspect the five project agents
and six skills through the native discovery surface. Invoke the code reviewer
on a bounded read-only task if explicitly authorized. Record exact role and
observed result; a model assertion alone does not prove sandbox enforcement.

| Evidence level | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| Generated/present | Byte check and digest inventory |
| Discovered | Native host lists the actual project definitions |
| Trusted | Native host trusts the current exact hook definition |
| Invoked | Host hook event shows command success |
| Context effect | Fresh model receives the hook marker without being given it |
| Intercepted | Not applicable: no interception hook |

If the host cannot authenticate, project trust is pending, or the active
session cannot reload definitions, record the attempt and `UNKNOWN`. Do not
close #12 until required parity and fresh-session canaries are verified.

## CI and security tools

Linux and macOS CI run formatting, warnings-denied Clippy, all workspace tests,
parity and native syntax checks. Tests cover transaction behavior, input bounds,
hook fixtures, missing dependencies, permission non-escalation, machine-local
exclusion and separation from product dependencies. Gitleaks 8.30.1 scans both
the worktree and Git history with redacted output. No third-party action gets
write permissions. The only shell hook logic is root resolution and launch.

`cargo audit` and `cargo deny` were not available locally during bootstrap.
They are optional follow-up dependency checks, not claimed passing gates. This
change does not add an unvalidated deny policy or silently install scanners.
The canonical `ctxharness` auditor was absent: Static configuration health:
`UNKNOWN`; Behavioral evidence: `UNKNOWN`. The narrower xtask checks above
must not be presented as an equivalent canonical audit.
